question: Why are old writings from figures like Hippocrates and Pliny so important to occupational health?

options.A: They established the first formal nursing schools in Europe
options.B: They proved that workplace injuries were caused by poor hygiene
options.C: They forced emperors to pass the first fair labor acts
options.D: They linked specific jobs directly to certain physical illnesses

explanation: These early scholars were the first to notice how certain jobs—like working with lead or sulfur—made workers sick. It laid the foundation for modern occupational health! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h1)

question: A coal miner has a chronic cough and trouble breathing after years underground. What caused this?

options.A: Inhalation and accumulation of dust particles in lung tissue
options.B: Bacterial infection spreading rapidly through the crowded workshop
options.C: Severe vitamin deficiency caused by working long shifts in the dark
options.D: Sudden allergic reaction to synthetic dyes used in the factory

explanation: Breathing in coal dust over many years causes it to build up in the lungs, leading to long-term damage and breathing difficulties. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h2)

question: What simple question did Bernardino Ramazzini say doctors must always ask their patients?

options.B: How many hours do you sleep?
options.C: Where do you buy your food?
options.D: What is your family medical history?

explanation: Ramazzini realized that a patient's job is often the biggest clue to what is making them sick. Always remember to check your patient's work background! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h3)

question: How did Alice Hamilton help make American factories safer?

options.A: By inventing heavy protective suits for miners and chemical workers
options.B: By collecting scientific field data on chemical poisonings and publishing her findings
options.C: By organizing violent labor strikes that forced factory owners to close down
options.D: By passing strict presidential executive orders without consulting scientists

explanation: Alice Hamilton used careful research to expose dangerous workplace poisons, convincing the public and lawmakers to make positive changes. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h3)

question: Who was one of the very first industrial visiting nurses in the US, starting with Procter & Gamble in 1895?
explanation: Ada Mayo Stewart provided great nursing care to workers and their families, setting an inspiring example for workplace health nurses. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h4)

question: Aside from treating cuts and bruises, what was another big focus for early industrial nurses?

options.A: Representing factory owners in legal disputes against injured workers
options.B: Addressing broader community health issues like tuberculosis and sanitation
options.C: Designing safer mechanical looms and steam engines for factory floors
options.D: Managing company financial accounts and payroll distribution

explanation: Early industrial nurses acted like community health champions, helping workers fight infectious diseases and improve their living conditions. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h4)

question: What was the main goal of introducing workers' compensation laws?

options.A: To fund free medical schools for aspiring occupational health nurses
options.B: To allow employers to fire injured workers immediately without paying severance
options.C: To punish factory owners by throwing them in prison for safety violations
options.D: To provide financial support for workers injured on the job without requiring lawsuits

explanation: Workers' comp ensured that staff hurt on the job got medical care and money for bills without having to go through stressful court battles. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h5)

question: How did modern safety acts like OSHA change workplace safety?

options.A: Establishing legally enforceable safety standards with power to inspect and fine workplaces
options.B: Banning the use of all heavy machinery in manufacturing and construction
options.C: Requiring all industrial workers to retire by age fifty with full pensions
options.D: Leaving workplace safety entirely up to the voluntary discretion of corporate boards

explanation: OSHA turned workplace safety from a nice idea into a strict legal duty, using inspections and fines to keep workers safe. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h5)

question: How has occupational health nursing changed from the 19th century to the 21st century?

options.A: From working exclusively in hospital wards to running corporate legal departments
options.B: From addressing traumatic physical injuries in heavy factories to managing chronic strain and mental wellness
options.C: From ignoring chemical exposures entirely to treating only rare tropical diseases
options.D: From focusing exclusively on boardroom management to supervising mining operations

explanation: While physical safety is still key, today's occupational nurses focus a lot on ergonomics, mental health, and preventing everyday work stress. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h6)

question: Office workers are complaining of severe back and wrist pain from poorly set up desks. What is the best intervention?

options.A: Immediate quarantine of the office building for suspected chemical leaks
options.B: Prescription of heavy industrial respirators to prevent indoor dust inhalation
options.C: Mandatory industrial safety harness training for all desk workers
options.D: Ergonomic workspace assessment and workstation adjustments

explanation: An ergonomic check helps fix poor posture, chair height, and computer placement, stopping strain before it gets worse! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h6)
